## A hub for sensor-based biodiversity monitoring {.turquoise}

[MANTIS will form the **connective tissue** for automated monitoring with novel technologies based on image and sound across Europe.]{.lede}

::: {.tight}
- **Connect data acquisition** – align protocols, deployments and annotations, and extend spatial and taxonomic coverage.  [Package 1]{.small}
- **Connect the data** – harmonise datasets and metadata into a quality-controlled flow from images and sounds to indicators, including transnational benchmarking of AI models.  [Package 2]{.small}
- **Connect the community** – link the users of these technologies to one another, and to the skills and resources that sustain a transnational effort.  [Package 3]{.small}
:::

[Aarhus University with the Nature Conservation Agency CZ · 1 January 2027 – 30 September 2028 · Core Activity 3 primary, Core Activities 2 and 4 secondary · a progenitor for a Thematic Hub associated with an EBOCC.]{.small}

::: {.notes}
45 seconds. Say what kind of thing MANTIS is before saying what it does:
infrastructure for monitoring itself, not another technology and not another
taxon's dataset. "Connective tissue" is the proposal's own phrase and the one
image worth repeating; the three bullets are the three packages, and they
return on the figure two slides from now.
:::

## Building a system for the European sensors {.blue}

[The devices are in the ground already – AMI traps and acoustic recorders across **11 countries** in the ABMS pilot (2.6.5), an AMI trap and a CamAlien unit in **10 countries** in the IAS pilot (2.6.2), acoustic recorders in **ten countries** in BiodivPond (2.6.8), **four countries** in TABMON, and insect camera traps in **over 30 countries** through MAMBO and related projects. They are operated as independent national efforts, and three bottlenecks follow – not one of them national.]{.lede}

::: {.tight}
1. **Verification cannot keep up.** Image and sound data has grown faster than the community's capacity to verify it, calibrate the AI models processing it, and make the outputs comparable across countries and taxa.
2. **AI accuracy is unknown outside its training context.** Moth classifiers trained on Danish and UK expert-verified images performed poorly in Slovakia, Croatia, Bulgaria and Israel.
3. **Sensors still need field visits.** A substantial share of deployed acoustic recorders require manual retrieval rather than remote transfer, limiting temporal coverage and cost-efficiency.
:::

> Left unaddressed, these problems risk automated monitoring becoming a source of fragmented, incomparable, or even unprocessed national data – repeating, at greater cost and complexity, the exact coordination problem transnational monitoring should be designed to solve.

::: {.notes}
90 seconds, and this is the slide that has to land. First half: nobody is being
asked to believe in an unproven technology, and Biodiversa+ has already paid
for a good share of these deployments. Second half: model calibration, sensor
connectivity and annotation protocol design are not country-specific technical
problems, so they should not be solved redundantly across up to 27 Member
States. Read the quote out – it is the proposal's own sentence.
:::

## Sustaining the System {.green}

> …national and regional automated monitoring efforts using image and sound technologies will function as a **connected, transnational system** rather than isolated national deployments.

::: {.tight}
- **One place every deployment is registered** – 100% of active AMI, CamAlien and acoustic deployments across ≥8 partner countries, machine-readable and Camtrap DP-compliant.  [O1 · 30 Sep 2028]{.small}
- **Sensor data reaching policy without bespoke analysis** – ≥4 indicators live on the MANTIS dashboard, each mapped to NRR Art. 10 / EU-PoMS, the Habitats or Birds Directive or IAS Regulation 1143/2014, auto-updating from GBIF.  [O2 · 30 Sep 2028]{.small}
- **Data to benchmark AI against** – ≥5,000 expert-verified annotations published under FAIR principles, ≥20% reviewed by experts from ≥2 countries.  [O3 · 31 Dec 2027]{.small}
- **Partners who can run this themselves** – 25 summer-school participants from ≥12 countries.  [O4 · 30 Jun 2028]{.small}
- **A pathway beyond Biodiversa+** – a roadmap endorsed by ≥2/3 of partners, naming ≥2 concrete funding or hosting pathways.  [O5 · 30 Jun 2028]{.small}
:::

[**€796,850.18 requested** – CORE + ENHANCED for the two leads (€422,535.30), plus ≈€54,494.36 for each of six additional participating partners. The activity descopes cleanly: fewer partners means proportionally fewer scaled deployments, not a thinner version of everything. Nothing here needs continued funding to survive 2028 – GitHub Pages and GBIF carry the outputs, and statutory Habitats and Birds Directive duties carry the verification capacity.]{.small}

::: {.notes}
90 seconds, and it serves two rooms at once. Every objective carries a date and
a threshold, so at the end of the activity you can tell whether it was met
without holding a discussion about it: O3 is the one everything else depends
on, O5 the one that decides whether this outlives the money. For a partner
weighing whether to join, the commitment behind the per-partner figure is four
person-months, two in-person attendances, and equipment that stays with you.
If asked about maintenance: no new secretariat and no hosting bill – NCA CZ
holds the reference datasets under its reporting duties, Aarhus underwrites
media storage to 2031, and the registration system and benchmarking transfer
to BiodivPond, ABMS and the IAS pilot.
:::

::: {.notes}
20 seconds, then questions. The likeliest three: why not leave this to the
pilots (they have no mandate or budget to work across each other); what if
fewer partners join (risk R2 – descope the scalable tier proportionally); and
what happens if verification runs late (risk R3 – a one-quarter buffer between
1.3 and 2.1, with annotation effort reallocated across partners). The long
version of any answer is in the full pitch on the hub site.
:::
